comments: Curlew next to an oystercatcher of which it was the same size.
Flew by very close to the seawall. Sterna type tern with obvious long tail streamers. Had to sacrifice getting a photo to protect my camera from the horrible weather.
Two juveniles, didn't see the third very well.
Two putative males together with Common Eiders. Surf Scoters werr separated from the big Velvet group!
The same group that seen by many birders  at the see wall!

Two males managed to glimpse with the tremendous flock of Velvets as they were getting closer to the shore after 19.00 pm. Distinctive bill shape from profile and the conspicous elongated white eyebrow mark help to separate them from Velvets at close range.
Adult drake, seen while scanning for other species. One of three being reported for weeks now.
We saw 1-2 in between many eiders
bird has been calling very actively recently, another bird heard calling in the distance at the same time

juv/female type flew north in morning. dark blackish brown duck, white secondaries obvious in flight, diffuse pale spots on face, concave bill structure
flew north with 5 bar tailed godwits

two juveniles flew north at 12:40 alongside dark phase arctic skua. one bird intermediate phase, one darker. Small skuas with narrow wings, notably smaller and lighter in structure than Arctic Skua, fairly long, attenutated tail. Plumage overall quite cold in told, limited white on base to primaries on underwing (less than neighbouring Arctic) and restricted white on upperwings also, uppertail coverts appeared pale. Intermediate phase bird had yellowish tone to collar and capped impression. overall impression was of small, cold toned skuas with comparatively delicate structure and impression reminscent of a kittiwake.
pale phase, spooned adult flew north in evening

presumably an individual that has been present in general area for some time. immature/female type, dark chocolate brown harrier with cream yellowish crown and throat patch. longer tail than buzzard which viewed alongside
